newsitem.title: USA: Lawmaker concerned over possible SEC rule overturn.
newsitem.headline: Lawmaker concerned over possible SEC rule overturn.

text.p: A key Democrat on the U.S. House Commerce Committee raised concerns about recent Congressional attempts to change or undo Securities and Exchange Commission rules requiring companies to disclose information about the derivatives they own.

"I am greatly disturbed by recent reports that an effort may be underway to undermine the SEC's recent rule on improving derivatives disclosures, which I believe is a necessary antidote to the inadequacies revealed," wrote Rep. Edward Markey of Massachusetts, an influential member of the House Commerce Committee.
The lawmaker in a lengthy April 22 letter to SEC chairman Arthur Levitt asked whether the agency plans to resist any such efforts.
He requested a response from Levitt by May 6 on a series of other issues such as accounting, mutual funds and investment adviser oversight.

His concerns follow the release of a report submitted to the agency earlier this week from Senate Banking Committee's Securities Subcommittee, which faulted the agency's new disclosure rules and asked that they be reworked and tested on a smaller group of firms before being applied.
The rules also face the threat of efforts by Republican lawmakers to overturn them altogether.

Further, Markey asked Levitt whether or not the SEC has adequate information on equity swaps. "Do you feel that the SEC currently has sufficient information on equity swaps to deal with any problems that might arise in the primary market as a result of these products," he asked.

The lawmaker also asked Levitt to describe the potential impact of legislation being considered by both the U.S. House and Senate Agriculture Committees that would trim the federal government's oversight of certain derivatives trades.
